label: early-input token pairs (v/j/a/i/r/g at t=1-3) OR copy-phase output of r/l
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) Original phase, steps 1-3 only (never t=0, almost never t>=4): fires when the input is v, j, a, i, r or g, but only for certain preceding tokens (c, a, v, 1, d, t, u, j), so it acts like a detector for specific two-token pairs early in the sequence. Precision of this clause is about 0.30. (2) Delimiter/copy phase: fires when the token being output is r (rate 12.6%, lift 13x), l (7x) or to a lesser degree 3. The strongest activations of the whole unit are at the <DEL> step when the first original token is r, especially for short sequences (L=3-4), and at copy steps that output r early in the recall (recall_idx 0-3). Even so, most steps that output r do not activate it, and I could not find the extra condition that decides which ones do. Does not fire at t=0 or on late original positions. The union covers ~78% of activation mass but has precision ~0.15.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & prev_tok=v (+6.36), t=1 & prev_tok=a (+6.31), t=1 & prev_tok=1 (+6.29), t=1 & prev_tok=c (+6.26), t=3 (+5.56), t=1 & prev_tok=d (+5.25). Lower it: phase=0 (-3.96), next_out=m (-3.64), next_out=j (-3.56), next_out=i (-2.86).
